title: The Smash of Determination and Love
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Haibara, Genta, Mitsuhiko, Ayumi, Inspector Tamana, Sergeant Kato) omitted by convention -- none of them carry case-specific motive/relationship data beyond their usual investigative function. Ran, Sonoko and Kogoro are kept in despite being recurring-cast, because in this episode they are not narrator furniture: Ran is the actual kidnap victim, Sonoko is the manipulation target the whole plot pivots on, and Kogoro is the specific target of the (fake) ransom call. case_type: attempted_murder. The old cases/ file's culprit (s3 Tachikawa Masato) is CONFIRMED correct against the transcript -- unlike some other rebuilds, this is not a case of a wrong or backwards culprit. What the old file missed entirely: Saeki (the scapegoated secretary whose suicide is the actual motive engine), Sonoko as a load-bearing character, Kogoro's ransom subplot, the steel-factory location doing double duty as both the conspirators' old workplace and Ran's present-day prison, and the kanji-misreading clue (Hirukomachi/Yokomachi) that actually finds her. One inference flagged as uncertain: Ran says she heard 'a third man's voice' before blacking out during the abduction, in addition to the two men (Doi, Mamiya) a witness saw carrying her off; the transcript does not name this third voice directly, but since Doi and Mamiya are later found already stationed at the factory watching the tournament on TV (never leaving it) while Tachikawa is the only conspirator unaccounted for and is separately revealed as the would-be assassin, the `assaults` edge for the head-strike is attributed to Tachikawa (p3) as the most consistent reading, not a directly quoted confession.

clues.desc: Billboard Ran reads over the phone sounds like 'Hirukomachi'; Sonoko's text names the same kanji as 'Yokomachi' -- same characters, different reading, pinpoints the factory.
Narimasu's bodyguards step back only during the trophy handoff, and today is Saeki's death anniversary -- whichever finalist wins gets the one unguarded moment.
